claims.text: Adding approximately 7 at% Zr to a NbTiAl-based refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical performance relative to a Zr-free baseline.
The Zr-free baseline is a homogeneous NbTiAl-based solid solution.
Homogenization near 1100 K will fully incorporate approximately 7 at% Zr as a solid-solution element.
Zr addition will produce atomic-scale lattice distortions uniformly throughout the alloy.
Zr atoms are oversized relative to the relevant host lattice sites.
Lattice strain generated by Zr will impede dislocation motion and provide solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed dislocation-obstacle effect will be particularly effective at 1023–1123 K.
The Zr addition will increase high-temperature yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the Zr-free baseline.
The Zr addition will improve creep resistance relative to the Zr-free baseline.
The Zr-modified alloy will preserve room-temperature mechanical properties, including ductility.
Adding approximately 7 at% Zr will not significantly increase the alloy density.
Significant deviation from the proposed Zr content may prevent the anticipated strengthening.
Inhomogeneous homogenization may cause secondary-phase precipitation and prevent the anticipated solid-solution strengthening.
Secondary-phase formation could compromise room-temperature performance.
